--- title: "[CensoringDistribution]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Kaplan-Meier estimate of the censoring distribution, providing IPC weights. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_ipcw.py#L56-L247){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python CensoringDistribution(surv) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The censoring distribution $\hat{G}(t) = P(\text{not censored by time } t)$ is the Kaplan-Meier estimator applied to the censoring process (where censoring is treated as the "event" and true events are treated as censoring). This is the foundation of all IPCW methods. IPC weights $w_i = 1 / \hat{G}(t_i^-)$ reweight observed subjects to represent the full population, correcting for the information lost to censoring. Subjects who experienced an event at a time when censoring was heavy receive larger weights (they represent more unobserved subjects), while subjects at times with little censoring receive weights near 1. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A right-censored `Surv` response. The censoring distribution is estimated from the observed censoring pattern. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Estimate the censoring distribution for the lung dataset: ::: {#6adec923 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") # Build the response from the named columns, then fit the censoring distribution y = gw.Outcome.surv(time="time", event="status").bind(lung) cens = gw.CensoringDistribution(y) cens ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` CensoringDistribution (n=228, censored=63) 60 unique censoring times, tail G = 0.0000 ``` ::: ::: Retrieve IPC weights for all subjects: ::: {#5898f5ca .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # IPC weights: larger where censoring is heavier weights = cens.weights() weights[:10] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` array([1.35885572, 1.59245456, 0. , 1.09235351, 3.8210638 , 0. , 1.35885572, 1.41273529, 1.10044502, 1.01015385]) ``` ::: ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
survival() Evaluate the censoring survival function $\hat{G}(t)$ at arbitrary times.
survival_left() Evaluate $\hat{G}(t^-)$, the left-continuous censoring survival.
to_frame() Return the censoring survival curve as a DataFrame.
weights() IPC weights $w_i = \delta_i / \hat{G}(t_i^-)$ for each subject.
### [survival()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Evaluate the censoring survival function $\hat{G}(t)$ at arbitrary times. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_ipcw.py#L112-L146){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python survival(times) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns the probability of not being censored by each requested time, estimated via the Kaplan-Meier estimator of the censoring distribution. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : 1-D array-like of query times. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : $\hat{G}(t)$ at each query time, shape `(len(times),)`. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Evaluate the probability of remaining uncensored at one year and two years: ::: {#e0506719 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") y = gw.Outcome.surv(time="time", event="status").bind(lung) cens = gw.CensoringDistribution(y) cens.survival([365, 730]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` array([0.69728182, 0.49350505]) ``` ::: ::: ### [survival_left()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Evaluate $\hat{G}(t^-)$, the left-continuous censoring survival. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_ipcw.py#L148-L183){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python survival_left(times) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} This is the censoring survival just before each time point, used for IPC weight construction. At the first observation time, $\hat{G}(t^-) = 1$. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : 1-D array-like of query times. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : $\hat{G}(t^-)$ at each query time, shape `(len(times),)`. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} The left-continuous version evaluates the censoring survival just before each time point, which is what IPC weights use as denominator: ::: {#7ee60ce2 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") y = gw.Outcome.surv(time="time", event="status").bind(lung) cens = gw.CensoringDistribution(y) cens.survival_left([365, 730]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` array([0.69728182, 0.49350505]) ``` ::: ::: ### ``` ::: ::: ### [weights()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} IPC weights $w_i = \delta_i / \hat{G}(t_i^-)$ for each subject. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_ipcw.py#L185-L215){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python weights(*, tau=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Uncensored subjects receive weight $1 / \hat{G}(t_i^-)$. Censored subjects receive weight 0 (they are excluded from the reweighted analysis). Subjects with events after `tau` also receive weight 0. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tau]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Truncation time. Subjects with event times after `tau` receive zero weight. Defaults to the maximum observed time. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : IPC weights, shape `(n,)`. :::
